uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of how fast UK consumer prices are rising. It is the figure the Bank of England's 2% target is judged against, and gilts, sterling and mortgage pricing move with it.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: The Office for National Statistics publishes the UK's September consumer price reading, which settles how fast prices rose over the month and where UK inflation stood as the summer ended.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Open Market Committee, the Federal Reserve's rate-setting body, which meets eight times a year to set the federal funds rate. It is the price of dollar credit worldwide, and borrowing costs from mortgages to emerging-market debt are indexed to it.
fomc-2026-10.recent: The committee raised rates 12-0 on September 16 because a closed strait pushed oil into US consumer prices, which rose 0.4% in August. Tightening into a supply shock is a choice it must make again with the strait still closed, and this time without the unanimity a first move buys. Trump has publicly called for lower rates.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council sets interest rates for the euro area and meets about every six weeks. Its deposit rate sets the cost of credit across the currency union, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-10.recent: The European Central Bank spent September on the banking system's plumbing. It wants MiCA's stablecoin yield ban extended to crypto lending and staking to stop deposits leaking out of banks, and it will hold tokenized securities on its own books. This meeting settles whether Frankfurt holds after the Fed and the Bank of Japan both raised rates.

boj-2026-10.standing: The Bank of Japan's Policy Board meets eight times a year to set the short-term policy rate. Its decisions set borrowing costs in one of the world's largest economies and move the yen, which carries them to yen-funded trades worldwide.
boj-2026-10.recent: This is the Bank of Japan's first meeting since its September hike to a 31-year high, which it made to curb rising prices. That hike came two days after the Fed tightened because of a closed strait, and the BOJ's balancing act with Bessent has only grown harder since. This meeting settles whether September was a single step or the start of a run.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, whose nine members vote individually on Bank Rate about eight times a year. It sets what British banks pay for reserves, and feeds through to mortgages, business lending and the pound.
boe-2026-11.recent: Brent settled near $106 a barrel this month, an imported cost no rate decision can reach — and other central banks have already moved on it: the Fed raised in a unanimous 12-0 vote, the Bank of Japan to 1.25%, a 31-year high. What this meeting settles is whether the households exposed to it pay for that supply shock twice.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Open Market Committee, the twelve-member body that sets the federal funds rate at eight scheduled meetings a year. It is the reference price for dollar credit worldwide, so borrowing costs from US mortgages to emerging-market debt move with it.
fomc-2026-12.recent: The committee raised rates 12-0 in September, tightening into a supply shock rather than a demand boom: Brent above $100 after the closure of a strait pushed August consumer prices up 0.4%. Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call before that vote, and the December meeting settles whether a war-driven price level is something this committee keeps chasing.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The yearly meeting of leaders from 19 countries, the European Union and the African Union. A presidency that rotates each year sets the agenda and the guest list. Its members produce most of the world's output and trade.
g20-2026-miami.recent: As host, Washington has invited Putin to Miami despite his ICC arrest warrant, and the Kremlin says it is considering it. European partners had called Russia's return to the G20 a red line. Zelensky has said he is ready to meet Putin face-to-face there, so the guest list is now the dispute.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets every six weeks to set interest rates for the whole euro area. Its deposit rate anchors what banks, households and governments pay to borrow, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-12.recent: The ECB has spent the weeks before this meeting on the plumbing of bank funding: it wants MiCA's stablecoin yield ban extended to crypto lending and staking, explicitly to stop deposits leaking out of banks, and it will hold blockchain-based bonds on its own books. The rate decision settles the other side of that ledger — what those deposits earn.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate — the floor under British mortgages, savings returns and government borrowing costs. Sterling and the gilt market move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: The Fed raised rates 12-0 into a supply shock and the Bank of Japan went to a 31-year high, both tightening against oil near $106 a barrel rather than against domestic demand. The committee meets into that same imported shock, and what it settles is how much of the cost lands on borrowers.

boj-2026-12.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set its short-term policy rate. After decades near zero, its moves reach savers, borrowers, the yen and the carry trades funded in it worldwide.
boj-2026-12.recent: This is the first meeting since the Bank of Japan raised rates to a 31-year high to curb rising prices. That tightening has to be squared with Washington: the balancing act with Bessent is only going to get harder, and this meeting settles whether the board keeps climbing or pauses to absorb the last move.

fred-us-gdp-2026-09-30.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's quarterly measure of everything the US economy produces, revised twice as fuller data arrive. It is the benchmark growth reading that interest-rate expectations, Treasury yields and the dollar are priced against.
fred-us-gdp-2026-09-30.recent: The release lands a week after the OECD said the U.S. economy will grow faster than its allies, on an AI investment boom that is offsetting a Middle East energy shock for now. The figures show how much of American output that spending is actually carrying, with the Nasdaq at an all-time high on the same bet.

fred-us-pce-2026-09-30.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's monthly report on US personal income and spending. Its PCE price index is the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, so it moves rate expectations, Treasury yields and the dollar.
fred-us-pce-2026-09-30.recent: The Bureau of Economic Analysis publishes US PCE with no recent reporting that sets this month apart from a routine one. The release settles the inflation reading that rate-setters weigh most heavily, along with what households earned and spent.

fred-us-jobs-report-2026-10-02.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly count of jobs added by US employers, published alongside the unemployment rate. Treasury yields, the dollar and interest-rate expectations all move within minutes of its release.
fred-us-jobs-report-2026-10-02.recent: The Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes the US jobs report, which settles how many jobs employers added over the month and where unemployment now stands.
